Word.PageSetup#bottomMargin.notes: Writes the addressed section page setup. Orientation is Portrait/Landscape; dimensions and margins use points with finite supported bounds. Assignments on one proxy coalesce, preserving other section properties. Runtime-local tracked layout edits refuse.

Word.Range#insertContentControl.notes: Creates RichText, PlainText, and DatePicker controls around an eligible single-paragraph range. Other types refuse. Sync before configuring the returned proxy. DatePicker creates a real date SDT; typed date configuration accessors remain unavailable. TrackMineOnly can wrap nonempty ordinary text in PlainText, RichText, or DatePicker controls outside collaboration. Accept keeps the control; Reject restores the original formatted text. The author can set the pending control’s tag and title. Empty ranges, existing review markup, and other control structure changes refuse. A range whose text moved since it was read refuses with StaleDocument. Inserting a control or paragraph inside a control and deleting that control with keepContent=false in one batch refuses with ConflictingChanges before writing.

Word.ContentControl#tag.notes: Writes the control metadata string while preserving its contents and other properties. The control must still exist and pass canonical protection/binding checks. While tracking, only the author of a pending inserted control can write this property.

Word.ContentControl#title.notes: Writes the control metadata string while preserving its contents and other properties. The control must still exist and pass canonical protection/binding checks. While tracking, only the author of a pending inserted control can write this property.

Word.ContentControl#delete.notes: With keepContent=true removes the wrapper while preserving its contents; false removes both. Protected, bound, or unsupported control structures refuse atomically. Inserting a control or paragraph inside a control and deleting that control with keepContent=false in one batch refuses with ConflictingChanges before writing. Deleting nested controls in one batch succeeds.

Word.ContentControl#cannotEdit.notes: Writes one lock axis without requiring a prior load. Assignments on the same proxy coalesce and preserve the other axis. Effective ancestor locks and bound controls remain enforced; this is not a protection bypass. A browser runtime over an editor created with contentLockPolicy.allowFormattingInLockedContent lets untracked font writes pass a content lock; text writes and tracked font writes still refuse. The server runtime does not take this option and refuses both, as Word does.

Word.ContentControl#cannotDelete.notes: Writes one lock axis without requiring a prior load. Assignments on the same proxy coalesce and preserve the other axis. Effective ancestor locks and bound controls remain enforced; this is not a protection bypass.

Word.Paragraph#insertParagraph.notes: TrackMineOnly records inserted text and the paragraph mark as native revisions. Reject removes both after save and reopen. Anchors with foreign, structural, or move revisions refuse. Insertion can continue the runtime author's text, paragraph, and formatting proposals. Other supported behavior uses the standard Before/After insertion locations. Text may contain \v, which inserts a manual line break (w:br); text reads report the break as \v, so read text can be written back. Other paragraph-mark characters refuse.

Word.Body#footnotes.notes: Enumerates distinct notes referenced within this body in reference order, including table-cell bodies. Separators and unreferenced notes are excluded. Dangling references and ambiguous note identities refuse. Note creation remains unsupported.

Word.Body#endnotes.notes: Enumerates distinct notes referenced within this body in reference order, including table-cell bodies. Separators and unreferenced notes are excluded. Dangling references and ambiguous note identities refuse. Note creation remains unsupported.

Word.Document#properties.notes: Core string properties: author, title, subject, keywords, comments, category, and read-only lastAuthor. Other properties, dates, and individual custom properties are not exposed. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#author.notes: Missing values read as empty strings. Writes accept XML-safe strings up to 4096 UTF-16 units, preserve unrelated properties, and commit at sync. TrackMineOnly writes refuse with NotSupported. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#title.notes: Missing values read as empty strings. Writes accept XML-safe strings up to 4096 UTF-16 units, preserve unrelated properties, and commit at sync. TrackMineOnly writes refuse with NotSupported. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#subject.notes: Missing values read as empty strings. Writes accept XML-safe strings up to 4096 UTF-16 units, preserve unrelated properties, and commit at sync. TrackMineOnly writes refuse with NotSupported. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#keywords.notes: Missing values read as empty strings. Writes accept XML-safe strings up to 4096 UTF-16 units, preserve unrelated properties, and commit at sync. TrackMineOnly writes refuse with NotSupported. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#comments.notes: Missing values read as empty strings. Writes accept XML-safe strings up to 4096 UTF-16 units, preserve unrelated properties, and commit at sync. TrackMineOnly writes refuse with NotSupported. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#category.notes: Missing values read as empty strings. Writes accept XML-safe strings up to 4096 UTF-16 units, preserve unrelated properties, and commit at sync. TrackMineOnly writes refuse with NotSupported. Collaborative writes require an existing core-properties part; create it before joining collaboration.

Word.DocumentProperties#lastAuthor.notes: Reads cp:lastModifiedBy after explicit load and sync. Missing values read as empty strings. This property has no setter.

Word.Document#removeDocumentInformation.notes: Only DocumentProperties removes standard core, extended, and custom property parts and their package relationships. Other modes, TrackMineOnly, and collaboration refuse with NotSupported. Run as the only write in its sync. Malformed or ambiguous part topology refuses before mutation. Content, comments, revisions, and media remain unchanged; this operation does not anonymize document content.

Word.Range#text.notes: Reads the range's text through its paragraph identity and offsets. A range whose text moved since it was read refuses with StaleDocument. Search again after an edit before the range's end in its paragraph.

Word.Range#font.notes: Reads and writes formatting through the range's paragraph identity and offsets. A range whose text moved since it was read refuses with StaleDocument.

Word.Range#getTextRanges.notes: Splits at the listed ending marks and at every paragraph end; a range never holds a paragraph mark. Boundaries use the model text that revisionTextView shows. Hidden text holds no ending mark, and ranges start and end at shown characters; hidden text between shown characters of one range stays inside it, so an edit through that range also changes it. A field, equation, picture, or note reference is one character that joins the word it touches; a field reads as its result text, and the others read as U+FFFC. A content control adds no boundary; a partial edit inside a content-locked control refuses with GeneralException and edit.protected-content, and a tracked deletion or replacement covering the whole control proposes removing it. Without trimSpacing each range keeps its trailing spacing, so plan deletions on those ranges, by index. trimSpacing removes spaces, tabs, and column breaks from range edges and drops ranges left empty. A tab ends a range only when listed. A range that view shows nothing of is omitted. At most 32 marks of at most 32 UTF-16 units. Each range is an exact span usable for insertText and delete in later syncs, also with TrackMineOnly, under the StaleDocument rule: edit from the end of a paragraph toward its start. Read ranges once before editing: after tracked edits, a range over pending revisions can join deleted and inserted text, and an edit that touches your own pending change refuses with NotImplemented and edit.tracked-own-pending-change. Read the proposed result with getReviewedText('Current'). Marks with an unpaired surrogate refuse with InvalidArgument.

Word.Paragraph#getTextRanges.notes: Same rules as Word.Range#getTextRanges, over the whole paragraph.

Word.Range#expandTo.notes: Answers the span from the earlier start to the later end, within one paragraph or across paragraphs of one story. Ranges in different stories refuse the sync with InvalidArgument. A range from another run refuses at the call with InvalidArgument. The answer follows the StaleDocument rule of Word.Body#getRange. expandToOrNullObject is not implemented.

Word.Range#getRange.notes: Whole and Content answer the same span; Start and End answer a collapsed range at that endpoint. After refuses with NotSupported, because a snapshot range never owns the position after its end. The answer is usable by a text write in the same sync.

Word.Range#getReviewedText.notes: Current drops pending deletions, move sources, and deleted paragraph marks; Original drops pending insertions, move destinations, and inserted paragraph marks. Kept paragraph marks read as a carriage return. Fields read as their displayed results. The default is Current. Formatting revisions do not change the text. Read-only; the document does not change.

Word.Paragraph#getReviewedText.notes: Same rules as Word.Range#getReviewedText, over the paragraph's own text.

Word.Range#search.notes: Searches within the range's paragraph identity and offsets. A range whose text moved since it was read refuses with StaleDocument. Each result range follows the same rule.

Word.Range#clear.notes: Clears the range's content through its paragraph identity and offsets. A range whose text moved since it was read refuses with StaleDocument.

Word.Body#getRange.notes: Answers a range through paragraph identities and offsets. A range whose text moved since it was read refuses with StaleDocument. A range that spans paragraphs, such as body.getRange('Whole'), also refuses when its first paragraph changed, when a paragraph between its ends changed, or when a paragraph was inserted or removed there. Get the range again after such an edit. In a very long session, a range read long ago can also refuse with StaleDocument when its history record was dropped; then expectedRevision can equal actualRevision although the range did not move. Read the range again.

Word.Paragraph#getRange.notes: Answers a range through the paragraph identity and offsets. The range refuses with StaleDocument after an edit before its end in that paragraph. Get the range again after such an edit.

OfficeExtension.Error#debugInfo.notes: DocxEditorError.debugInfo has code, message, errorLocation, and innerError. errorLocation is the consumer-facing path of the refused call. statement, surroundingStatements, and fullStatements are not provided.

OfficeExtension.DebugInfo#innerError.notes: innerError is present only when the engine names a specific reason. It is an object with a stable public diagnostic code, such as edit.tracked-operation-unsupported, and the fixed hint for that code as message. It never contains document content.

Word.Range#insertBookmark.notes: Names compare without case and follow the authoring rules: a letter or underscore first, then letters, digits, and underscores, at most 40 characters; other names fail context.sync() with InvalidArgument, and the batch writes nothing. The call itself does not throw, so an argument error reports at the sync like every other batch error. Names are unique in the whole document: a same-name bookmark moves here, also from another story (header, footer, or note), in the same sync. With TrackMineOnly the markers are written directly, because bookmarks are not revisions. Moving or deleting markers inside content-locked or bound controls refuses the whole transaction.

Word.Range#getBookmarks.notes: Answers names in document order. A non-empty range holds bookmarks it shares text with and point bookmarks inside it or at its start; an empty range holds the bookmark around it. includeAdjacent adds bookmarks that only touch an end; includeHidden adds names starting with an underscore. Markers between blocks (outside any paragraph) are not counted.

Word.Document#deleteBookmark.notes: Searches the main text, then headers, footers, and notes, and selects the first bookmark with the name, compared without case. Removes all same-name marker pairs in that bookmark's XML part; copies in other parts remain. The text stays. A missing name changes nothing. The removal joins the batch's transaction in any story, so it can share a sync with writes to another story. Moving or deleting markers inside content-locked or bound controls refuses the whole transaction.

Word.Document#getBookmarkRange.notes: Searches the main text, then headers, footers, and notes, compared without case. A missing name fails the sync with ItemNotFound. The range is a snapshot like every Range in this API.

Word.Document#getBookmarkRangeOrNullObje.notes: As getBookmarkRange, but a missing name answers a null object instead of failing.

Word.Bookmark#delete.notes: Removes same-name marker pairs in the bookmark's XML part and keeps the text. Copies in other parts remain. A bookmark the document no longer declares refuses with InvalidObjectPath.

OfficeExtension.LoadOption#select.notes: Collections accept items/<property> paths in load(...) strings, arrays, and select. collection.load('text') is treated as collection.load('items/text'). Items and the selected item properties load in the same context.sync(). As with every read in a sync, item properties report the document from before that sync's writes. Only one navigation level is supported: deeper paths such as items/font/bold, and navigation paths on objects that are not collections, refuse with InvalidArgument and name the path in target. items/<navigation property> such as items/font also refuses; load font on each item. On the range collection that Paragraph#split returns, item paths, top, and skip apply to the split's answer after its sync; before it, they refuse with NotImplemented. The object form with boolean property flags and $all is not accepted; use select.

Word.Paragraph#search.notes: Searches within one paragraph and accepts the same search options as Body#search. Text reads and matches use the runtime's revision text view. A paragraph from getFirst or getLast can be searched in the sync that resolves it.

Word.Table#mergeCells.notes: Merges the rectangle that the cells at (topRow, firstCell) and (bottomRow, lastCell) span. Cell indexes count each row's own cells, as rows/cells list them, so a merged cell counts once in its row. bottomRow must not be above topRow; either cell can lie further left. The rectangle grows to whole merged cells. A cell that crosses its edge, or a rectangle of one cell, refuses with InvalidArgument and the diagnostic code edit.table-merge-not-rectangle. The top-left cell takes w:gridSpan and w:vMerge and keeps the content of every non-empty cell in reading order. Returns the merged cell, which takes edits in the same sync. Cells with a pending cell revision refuse with NotImplemented. A legacy w:hMerge table and rows the grid cannot place refuse with InvalidArgument. TrackAll and TrackMineOnly refuse with NotSupported, because a merge has no tracked form. Supports collaboration, undo/redo, reconnect, and save/reopen. Text a participant types into an empty cell while a peer merges it away is discarded, as text typed into an empty paragraph a peer deletes is. Concurrent merges, splits, and column edits of one table converge, but can leave a row that ends before the last grid column. Column edits keep that row ending where it does, and a merge or split that needs its missing part refuses.

Word.TableCell#split.notes: Splits the cell into rowCount by columnCount cells, each from 1 to 63. Columns get equal widths: a new boundary within 20 twips of a grid boundary uses it, any other boundary cuts the grid column, and cells in other rows widen their w:gridSpan to keep their width. A cell merged over several rows splits only into a divisor of its rows; a one-row cell adds rows to the table, and the other cells of its row continue into them through w:vMerge. The first new cell keeps the content. Counts the cell cannot take refuse with InvalidArgument and the diagnostic code edit.table-split-unsupported: a row count that does not divide a merged cell's rows, columns narrower than the minimum column width, or, in a table without w:tblGrid, a column count that does not divide the columns the cell spans. Cells with a pending cell revision refuse with NotImplemented. TrackAll and TrackMineOnly refuse with NotSupported. Supports collaboration, undo/redo, reconnect, and save/reopen, with the concurrency limits described for Word.Table#mergeCells.

Word.Range#contentControls.notes: Lists every content control the range overlaps, at any nesting depth, in document order: an inline control that shares at least one character with the range, a control that holds the whole range, and a block control that holds one of its paragraphs. A collapsed range lists the controls at or around its position. Load items/cannotEdit, items/tag, and items/text to learn what an edit through the range would touch. getById, getByTag, and getByTitle search the same list.

Word.Paragraph#contentControls.notes: Same rules as Word.Range#contentControls over the whole paragraph: every inline control in it, at any depth, and each block control that holds it.
